desc: Real-time capture of Workload Tracker samples
r: nvme-solidigm-workload-tracker - Real-time capture of Workload Tracker samples

Captures and displays real-time workload tracker samples for the given Solidigm NVMe device. This command allows for monitoring and analysis of the device’s workload characteristics.

The <device> parameter is mandatory and may be either the NVMe character device (ex: /dev/nvme0), or a namespace block device (ex: /dev/nvme0n1).

<dl><dt data-o="">-e, --enable</dt><dd>Enable the workload tracker before capturing samples.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-d, --disable</dt><dd>Disable the workload tracker after capturing samples.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-s <time>, --sample-time=<time></dt><dd>Set the sample interval. Valid values are: default, 1ms, 5ms, 10ms, 50ms, 100ms, 500ms, 1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 1m, 5m, 10m, 30m, 1h.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-t <type>, --type=<type></dt><dd>Set the tracker type. Valid types are: Base, CmdQ, Pattern, RandSeq, Throttle, Power, Defrag.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-r <seconds>, --run-time=<seconds></dt><dd>Limit runtime capture time in seconds.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-f <count>, --flush-freq=<count></dt><dd>Number of samples (1 to 126) to wait before extracting data. Default is 100 samples.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-w, --wall-clock</dt><dd>Log current wall timestamp when entry was retrieved.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-T <field>, --trigger-field=<field></dt><dd>Field name to stop trigger on.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-V <value>, --trigger-threshold=<value></dt><dd>Field value to trigger stop sampling.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-D, --trigger-on-delta</dt><dd>Trigger on delta to stop sampling.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-L, --trigger-on-latency</dt><dd>Use latency tracker to trigger stop sampling.</dd></dl> <dl><dt data-o="">-v, --verbose</dt><dd>Increase logging verbosity. Can be used multiple times.</dd></dl>

•Enable the workload tracker and capture samples: 
# nvme solidigm workload-tracker /dev/nvme0 --enable
•Capture workload tracker samples with a 1ms interval for 60 seconds: 
# nvme solidigm workload-tracker /dev/nvme0 --enable --sample-time=1ms --run-time=60
•Disable the workload tracker: 
# nvme solidigm workload-tracker /dev/nvme0 --disable
•Enable the workload tracker and capture samples with a specific sample time and type: 
# nvme solidigm workload-tracker /dev/nvme0 --enable --sample-time=1ms --type=Base
•Capture Power tracker samples with a 10-second interval for 5 minutes: 
# nvme solidigm workload-tracker /dev/nvme0 --enable --type=Power --sample-time=10s --run-time=300
